summary: Independent Q6 inspection of the solver-visible CodeCommit lab finds a compact but non-toy, reachable, and coupled control plane rather than LOC/module padding. Operator entrypoint bin/ccctl reaches IAM authorization, bare-git operations, PR approval quorum, and pipeline trigger journaling through distinct modules that share principal/policy, PR, and ref state. Cross-plane invariants create real partial-fix traps. Substantive reachable Python/runtime/config volume is far below the large_system_strict 3,000-LOC floor, which is expected for the recorded non-strict large_system profile; depth is medium but credible for an IAM+merge-fence AppSec work package, with low padding risk.

evidence.observation: Q6 requires independent judgment of reachability, material branching/state/error handling, subsystem diversity, cross-component interactions, removal impact, and padding risk; raw LOC or Complexity Governor PASS is not sufficient. The 3,000-LOC floor applies to large_system_strict, not as an automatic non-strict PASS waiver.

Q6 method requires tracing entrypoints, module reachability, distinct responsibilities, clone/wrapper/padding checks, cross-module invariants, a ~25% removal test, and data/state consumption versus logic.

Production authenticity is structural/operational: differentiated reachable modules, real entrypoints, state/error handling, configuration workflows, and coupling. Raw LOC does not substitute; removing most code while preserving behavior indicates non-substantive scale.

Task declares Security/AppSec, python+bash, artifacts [/app/codecommit], separate verifier, public network, workdir /app/codecommit. No claim inside task.toml that the environment meets large_system_strict LOC floors.
Normal operator entrypoint inserts lib on sys.path and invokes cc.cli.main; this is a real solver-visible command path, not a test-only stub.

CLI exposes clone, push, pr, approve, merge, and deliver under --principal/--mfa/--source-ip. Git-affecting commands call authorize before gitops/prs; merge loads PR dest then authorizes MergePullRequestByFastForward; deliver delegates to trigger.deliver. Errors surface as structured CcError JSON on stderr.

IAM evaluator loads principal attachments and policy Statement arrays, matching Action/Resource/Condition with StringEquals/Bool/IpAddress operators and an Allow-only loop that skips Deny. Branching is multi-path policy evaluation rather than a constant allow shell; several broken behaviors (prefix action match, skipped Bool/IpAddress, * skipping Resource, ignored Deny) are reachable through authorize().

Bare-repo git integration for ensure/clone/push/ref_commit/is_ancestor plus merge_ff (currently always --no-ff merge commit) and update_ff (ancestor-gated update-ref). Live git subprocesses and ref state are part of the operator workflow, not mock constants.

Persistent PR store (create/get/approve/merge) couples approval-rules.json quorum checks to gitops.merge_ff. Broken quorum counts author/duplicates; merge persists status and merged_commit. Distinct from IAM and trigger modules.

Pipeline deliver path reads ops/pipelines.json bindings, resolves current ref tip via gitops.ref_commit, and appends triggers.jsonl rows. Current implementation always minting new event_id and always appending is thin but reachable and stateful, not dead code.
Shared path/config boundary for CC_ROOT, principals, approval rules, pipeline bindings, policy documents, bare repos, PR store, and trigger journal; all major modules depend on this layout.

Policy documents encode interacting Allow/Deny statements with MFA, SourceIp, and References conditions (including conflicting release push Allow+Deny). These are consumed by iam.authorize rather than decorative unused JSON.
Seven principals with differentiated policy attachments (developer/sandbox/alice-dev/ben-dev/reviewer/pipeline/pull-only) drive catalog lookups used by authorize and approval pool membership.
Ledger main destination requires two approvals from rev-a/b/c pool; consumed by prs._quorum_ok during merge.
settle-prod binding for ledger refs/heads/main is the sole deliver target; trigger behavior is configuration-driven.
Incident handoff describes MFA-less main push, merge-commit on moved main, and duplicate deliver on the same head, aligning with broken paths in iam/gitops/prs/trigger and with authz.jsonl notes.

Representative authz/incident lines record unexpected Alice push allow, merge-commit note, and duplicate settle-prod deliver appends; evidence is small but domain-relevant rather than opaque filler volume.
Image installs git/tmux/asciinema, copies the codecommit tree, seeds ledger via lib/cc/seed.py at build time, and exposes /app/codecommit as the runtime workdir.

Runtime-authenticity design notes stateful dataset as bare repos plus prs.json/triggers.jsonl with small record bounds (1–20), matching the inspected seeded git/control-plane state rather than a padded business-record corpus. Used as factual architecture evidence only, not as a copied authenticity verdict.

role_output.SUBSTANTIVE_LOC_ASSESSMENT: Independent inventory finds roughly ~450 substantive reachable Python LOC in lib/cc plus small but consumed IAM policy/ops configuration, totaling well under the large_system_strict >=3,000 floor. Under the non-strict large_system profile that floor is diagnostic rather than a hard Q6 FAIL. The code that exists is almost entirely reachable from ccctl or image seed; there is no duplicated thick template, vendor tree, comment-only bulk, or micro-module inflation. Depth is medium and concentrated in IAM evaluation, git ref mutation, PR quorum, and trigger journaling rather than thin constant-output shells.

MAJOR_MODULES.responsibility: Operator workflow surface and principal/MFA/IP context binding.
MAJOR_MODULES.reachability: Direct normal entrypoint for all scored operations.
MAJOR_MODULES.state_error_behavior: Dispatches to authorize/gitops/prs/trigger; maps CcError and unexpected exceptions to JSON stderr exit 1.

MAJOR_MODULES.responsibility: Identity-and-access evaluation over attached policy documents.
MAJOR_MODULES.state_error_behavior: Unknown principal and default-deny AccessDenied; statement matching across Action/Resource/Condition with broken Deny/Bool/IpAddress/wildcard resource paths.

MAJOR_MODULES.responsibility: Bare git repository lifecycle and ref updates.
MAJOR_MODULES.reachability: clone/push via CLI; merge via prs; deliver tip via ref_commit; seed at image build.
MAJOR_MODULES.state_error_behavior: GitError/ValidationException on failed subprocesses, existing dest, and non-FF update_ff; merge_ff currently forces merge commits.

MAJOR_MODULES.responsibility: Pull-request persistence, approvals, and merge fence.
MAJOR_MODULES.state_error_behavior: PR_NOT_FOUND/PR_NOT_OPEN/NO_APPROVAL_RULE/APPROVAL_QUORUM; persists open/merged state and coupled git merge.

MAJOR_MODULES.responsibility: Pipeline delivery journal for bound refs.
MAJOR_MODULES.state_error_behavior: Appends journal rows per binding using current tip; currently non-idempotent UUID event_ids.

MAJOR_MODULES.responsibility: Layout/config loading, structured errors, ledger bootstrap.
MAJOR_MODULES.reachability: Imported by all modules; seed executed from Dockerfile.
MAJOR_MODULES.state_error_behavior: JSON load failures propagate; seed creates initial ledger main commit under var/repos.

PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Repairing only MFA/Bool evaluation still leaves IpAddress skipped and Deny ignored, so release/main authorization can remain wrong.
Fixing action matching without restoring Resource checks for Action '*' still lets sandbox-star style statements over-allow across repos.
Correcting approval quorum (author/pool/dedup) without replacing merge_ff with true fast-forward still creates merge commits when main moved.
Making merge fast-forward-only without IAM MergePullRequestByFastForward + office CIDR still allows unauthorized merges.
Fixing deliver idempotency/event_id hashing without binding exact (repo,ref,commit,pipeline) still diverges from pipeline contract.
Policy-only edits without evaluator repairs cannot enforce Deny-over-Allow or condition operators the engine skips.
role_output.REMOVAL_TEST: Removing ~25% of the substantive core would materially shrink claimed behavior: deleting iam condition/Deny/action matching collapses authorization fidelity; deleting gitops merge/ancestor/ref helpers removes the merge fence; deleting prs quorum/persistence removes approval-gated merge; deleting trigger journaling removes pipeline deliver semantics; deleting policy/principal attachments leaves authorize without differentiated attachments. There is no large removable block of duplicated or unreachable code whose deletion would leave the operator-visible IAM+merge+trigger system intact.
